# New renderings chosen in iliad-075 (Iliad 12.277–377)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ὣς ἔφατ’, οὐδ’ ἀπίθησε μέγας Τελαμώνιος Αἴας (12.364, whole line) | "So he spoke, and did not disobey, great Telamonian Ajax." | "So he spoke, and great Telamonian Ajax did not disobey." | "Ajax, son of Telamon", "greater Ajax"; built on the table's ὣς ἔφατ’, οὐδ’ ἀπίθησε … rows (2.166, 5.767) with μέγας "great" and Τελαμώνιος Αἴας "Telamonian Ajax" |
| ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας ἀπέβη Τελαμώνιος Αἴας (12.370) | "So then, having spoken, went away Telamonian Ajax," | "So he spoke, and Telamonian Ajax went off," | "departed", "left"; follows the table's ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας ἀπέβη κορυθαίολος Ἕκτωρ (iliad-037, iliad-039) with the name changed |
| αὐτίκ’ Ὀϊλιάδην ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (12.365, whole line) | "At once to Oileus’-son winged words he spoke:" | "At once he spoke winged words to the son of Oileus:" | "to Oileus’ son" in `l` (Ὀϊλιάδης is a patronymic and takes the hyphen, like Ἀτρεΐδης "Atreus’-son"); built on αὐτίκ’ Ἀθηναίην ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (4.69) |
| ἱπποκόμος (ἱπποκόμων τρυφαλειῶν, 12.339) | "horse-plumed" | "with horsehair plumes" | "horse-haired" (kept for ἱπποδάσεια), "horse-maned" (ἱππιοχαίτης), "crested" (λόφος), "plumed" alone (ἵππουρις); ἵππος + κόμη "hair" |
| πύκα θωρηκτάων (Λυκίων πύκα θωρηκτάων, 12.317) | "closely corseleted" | "closely corseleted" | "stoutly armoured", "well-armoured", "close-fitting" (each decides what πύκα says of the corselets); πύκα "closely, thickly", θωρηκτής from θώραξ "corselet"; the note says what πύκα means here is not known |
| ἔξαιτος (οἶνον ἔξαιτον, 12.320) | "choice" | "choice" | "special", "select", "picked" alone; ἐξαιτέω "ask out", so "picked out" in sense; "choice" is the one English word for it |
| λωτοῦντα (πεδία λωτοῦντα, 12.283; contracted from λωτόεντα) | "lotus-growing" | "lotus-growing" | "clover-grown" (the plant is decided elsewhere, ἐρεπτόμενοι 2.776), "lotus-bearing"; λωτός "lotus", the fodder plant of the table |
| προβοάω (προβοῶντε, 12.277, dual participle) | "shouting forth" | "calling out loud" | "shouting before", "crying in front" (each decides the prefix); the note says the prefix may mean "aloud" or "in front" |
| κοιρανέω (κοιρανέουσιν, of kings who are not inglorious, 12.318) | "act as rulers" | "rule" | "lord it" (the Odyssey’s, a swagger, which οὐκ ἀκλεέες rules out; a departure like 2.207, 4.230 for the same reason), "play the lord" |
| τόξων ἐῢ εἰδώς (12.350 = 12.363, of Teucer in a command) | "well knowing the bow" | "who knows the bow well" | the table's i "who knew the bow well" (2.718, 4.196), which suits a past-tense story; here the verb stands in a present-tense command, so the tense follows the sentence and the order of the words stays |
| κακότητα φέροντες (12.332) | "evil bringing" | "bringing misfortune" | "ruin" (kept for ἀρήν), "wickedness", "baseness"; the table's κακότης "misfortune" (10.70–71, "evil, heavy" in `l`) |
| ἀρήν (ἀρὴν ἑτάροισιν ἀμύναι, 12.334) | "ruin" | "ruin" | not new: the Odyssey's ἀρὴν ἀπὸ οἴκου ἀμῦναι "to ward ruin off", here with a dative of the people helped ("for his companions") instead of ἀπό |
| πρών (πρώονας ἄκρους, 12.281–282) | "spur" | "spurs" | "headlands" (kept for ἀκτή), "promontories"; "spur" is the one word for the jutting foot of a hill |
| ῥάβδος (ῥάβδοισι, 12.295–296, of the rods on the shield) | "rod" | "rod" | "staff", "wand" |
| πυροφόρος (ἀρούρης πυροφόροιο, 12.314) | "wheat-bearing" | "wheat-bearing" | "wheat-growing"; πυρός is wheat |
